paper_title: Searching for solar axions using data from the Sudbury Neutrino Observatory
coupling_convention: |g_aN^3| isovector axion-nucleon coupling in GeV^-1, exactly as plotted on the y-axis
notes: Paper derives a model-independent 95% CL exclusion on the isovector axion-nucleon coupling |g3_aN| > 2e-5 GeV^-1 from axion-induced deuteron dissociation using the full SNO dataset. The bound is essentially mass-independent for axion masses up to ~5.5 MeV (encoded as a flat two-point line from 1e-22 eV, the lower edge of the paper's Fig. 1 axis, to 5.5e6 eV). The exclusion has an upper ceiling of ~1e-3 GeV^-1 due to solar trapping (couplings above this escape the bound). Coupling type set to AxionNeutron per the generic-nucleon convention, since the paper constrains the isovector combination of g_an and g_ap; absent fine-tuned cancellation it applies to both g_an and g_ap individually. Values are emitted in GeV^-1 as quoted; multiply by m_n ≈ 0.939 GeV to obtain the dimensionless pseudoscalar coupling. Not a dark-matter search (solar axion flux), so no DM density assumed. | selector: figure_vision over text (quality (1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 0, 0.8, 42)) | Vision: Paper's main result is the blue SNO region: model-independent exclusion of the isovector axion-nucleon coupling |g_aN^3| between 2e-5 and 1e-3 GeV^-1 for axion masses up to ~5.5 MeV (values stated explicitly in text and confirmed on Fig. 1). Boundary is mass-independent (flat at 2e-5 GeV^-1) until the deuteron-dissociation kinematic endpoint near 5.5 MeV, where it rises steeply to the solar trapping ceiling of 1e-3 GeV^-1; the shape of this upturn is read approximately from the right edge of the plot. Coupling is the ISOVECTOR nucleon combination g_aN^3 = g_ap - g_an (plotted alongside g_an constraints from other experiments); classified as AxionNeutron per the generic-nucleon rule, but note it is not a pure neutron coupling. Not a dark-matter search (solar axion flux), so no DM density assumption.
